summary.title: Announcing third-party code scanning tools: static analysis & developer security training
summary.one_liner: GitHub announces 10 third-party SAST and code analysis tools that plug into GitHub code scanning, with results ingested via SARIF and shown in the native Security tab.
keywords: how to add security scanning to github pull requests
takeaways: GitHub code scanning is powered by CodeQL and can be extended with third-party tools while keeping one developer experience and API.
Third-party tools run as a GitHub Action or GitHub App triggered by events such as pull requests, then upload SARIF results to the Security Alerts tab.
GitHub aggregates alerts per tool and tracks and suppresses duplicate alerts.
The post lists 10 providers (e.g. Checkmarx, Codacy, CodeScan, Veracode, Synopsys, ShiftLeft, Muse, Xanitizer) and points to GitHub Marketplace to get started.
summary.summary: This 2020 GitHub blog announcement introduces ten third-party tools that integrate with GitHub code scanning, a feature powered by the CodeQL engine and extensible via the SARIF-based code scanning API. It explains the workflow: a GitHub Action or App runs on an event like a pull request, results are converted to SARIF and uploaded to the Security Alerts tab, and GitHub aggregates and deduplicates alerts. The rest of the page is a provider-by-provider list (Checkmarx, Codacy, CodeScan, DefenseCode ThunderScan, Fortify on Demand, Muse, Secure Code Warrior, ShiftLeft, Synopsys, Veracode, Xanitizer), each with a short description of its capabilities and a GitHub Marketplace link. The page is mostly vendor descriptions, so specific tool features are taken from the vendors' own blurbs.
